newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Seven-year-old kidnap victim killed in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Seven-year-old kidnap victim killed in Colombia.

text.p: The lifeless body of a seven-year-old boy was dumped on the doorstep of his home in southwestern Colombia on Thursday, three days after he was kidnapped and his family failed to come up with a ransom, police said.

Victor Alejandro Alvarez, the son of a shopkeeper from the town of Popayan, was snatched on his way to school on Monday. His captors, who had demanded $10,000 for his release, beat and strangled him to death, police said.
The kidnappers had been silent since Tuesday when they demanded the ransom and the boy's cash-strapped family had demanded, in turn, proof he was still alive, a police spokesman said.

No proof was provided and the boy's body was discovered on the doorstep of his home at 4:30 a.m. after his father was awakened by an anonymous phone call. Initial examinations indicated the child may have been murdered on the day he was abducted, the spokesman said.

Even in a country that boasts the highest abduction rate in the world -- with more than 110 minors snatched this year alone -- the brutality of the Popayan crime shocked the nation. It was the second case involving a child kidnapped and then killed in two months.

Dario Arizmendi, a leading commentator on the Caracol radio news network, urged listeners to join in a previously scheduled march in Bogota on Sunday to protest against Victor Alejandro's murder and the tide of kidnappings.
"We cannot remain asleep in the face of such a terrifying crime," he said.

More than 1,150 people were kidnapped in Colombia last year and over 900 have been abducted so far in 1996, according to Pais Libre, an independent group that counsels kidnap victims and their families and is the main organiser of Sunday's protest.
Roughly half of the kidnappings are carried by leftist guerrillas seeking to raise money for their war against the state.
